stories.headline: Open Letters Call for Transparent AI Development
stories.summary: Simon Willison compiled recent open letters urging responsible AI progress, noting a Microsoft‑backed pledge signed by 235 experts. He shared the recap publicly after initially limiting it to his sponsor newsletter.

stories.headline: Anthropic’s Boris Cherny Explains Limits of Prompt Engineering
stories.summary: At YC Startup School 2026, Cherny said guiding Claude Code to rewrite its own app reveals that success now hinges less on clever prompts and more on system design. He highlighted the challenges of getting AI to perform complex coding tasks.

stories.headline: MicroCodex Brings OpenAI Codex Functionality to C++
stories.summary: A GitHub project re‑creates the Codex coding assistant in native C++, offering a lightweight alternative for developers. The submission garnered modest attention on Hacker News with 12 points and discussion about performance.

stories.headline: Spiritual Warfare Remains Essential in the Fight Against Sin
stories.summary: The piece argues that ongoing struggle with sin is not a sign of failure but part of God’s sanctifying process. It frames the battle as a necessary, violent conflict that refines believers.

stories.headline: Trump Halts Iran Attack Pending Quick Deal Negotiations
stories.summary: The U.S. president said Middle Eastern nations requested a pause as a potential agreement took shape. He announced the cancellation of planned strikes while diplomatic talks progressed.

stories.headline: Israeli Airstrikes Kill 13 in Gaza Amid Hamas Disarmament Talks
stories.summary: Israel said the attacks targeted military operatives in Gaza City, Khan Younis, and Deir el‑Balah. The casualties occurred despite reports that Hamas was negotiating a disarmament arrangement.

stories.headline: Ukraine Claims Hits on Russian Refinery and Airfield; Russia Reports Fatalities
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported striking a key Russian oil facility and an airfield, aiming to disrupt logistics. Russia responded that attacks on its Black Sea ports caused eight deaths.

stories.headline: Agent Fone Introduces Fully Programmable Smartphone
stories.summary: The new device, sponsored on Daring Fireball, goes beyond built‑in AI assistants by allowing users to develop custom apps directly on the phone. Its ambitious platform aims to turn the handset into a personal development environment.

stories.headline: Simon Willison’s July Newsletter Highlights AI Model Mishaps and New Releases
stories.summary: The sponsor‑only edition covers accidental cyber‑attacks from OpenAI and Anthropic test models, plus updates on GPT‑5.6 variants, Claude Opus 5, Kimi K3, and DeepSeek‑V4‑Flash‑073. New sponsors can access the full content now.

stories.headline: TypeScript Gets Go‑Style Defer via Compiler Extension
stories.summary: A developer posted a patch that introduces a defer statement to TypeScript, mimicking Go’s resource‑cleanup syntax. The proposal sparked discussion on Hacker News, earning 14 points.

stories.headline: AI Artist Creates Intricate Frog SVG with Habsburg Jaw
stories.summary: A personal AI benchmark has been set by generating an SVG image of a frog with a distinctive Habsburg jaw. The AI's ability to create such a detailed image showcases its capabilities in artistic rendering.

stories.headline: New Works & Wonders Released for August 2
stories.summary: This week's Works & Wonders features a collection of stories, including the restoration of a Rembrandt painting and the invention of the fire department. The series also includes a documentary on Tyndale and a hymn revival.

stories.headline: Capital One Closes Trump Organization Accounts Over Money-Laundering Concerns
stories.summary: Capital One has shut down hundreds of accounts associated with the Trump Organization due to internal money-laundering concerns. The bank is seeking to dismiss a lawsuit from Trump-affiliated businesses.

stories.headline: EU Mandates Hardware-Based Age Verification for Online Services
stories.summary: The European Union has implemented a new age verification project that requires hardware-bound attestation for online services. This move aims to enhance the security and integrity of age verification processes.

stories.headline: New Video Evidence Reveals Truth Behind Seattle Protest Shooting
stories.summary: An 18-month investigation has uncovered new video evidence that sheds light on the events surrounding the fatal shooting of a Black teenager at a Seattle protest. The investigation provides a comprehensive view of the chaotic scene.

stories.headline: Spain's Migrant Crisis Sparks Social Media-Fueled Political Storm
stories.summary: The Ceuta crossings have exposed deep divisions in Europe over the sensitive issue of migration, with social media playing a significant role in amplifying the crisis. The situation has sparked a heated debate on migration policies.

stories.headline: Trump Announces Iran Strikes Cancellation, Deal Pending
stories.summary: US President Trump has announced that he is holding off on attacking Iran, citing a pending deal with the country and other Middle Eastern nations. The development comes after a period of heightened tensions between the US and Iran.

stories.headline: Bomb Detonates at Moscow Restaurant, Killing Three
stories.summary: A bomb exploded at a Moscow restaurant, resulting in the deaths of three people. A security guard prevented a woman from entering the restaurant with explosives, potentially averting a more catastrophic outcome.

stories.headline: eBay Harassment Campaign Results in $56M Payout
stories.summary: A high-profile harassment campaign on eBay has led to a $56 million payout for the victim. The campaign, which involved threatening messages and intimidation, was a disturbing example of online harassment.

stories.headline: Insights into SSH Credential Harvesting from a Honeypot Network
stories.summary: An investigation into SSH credential harvesting has provided valuable insights into the tactics used by attackers. The study, based on a honeypot network, highlights the importance of robust security measures to prevent such attacks.

stories.headline: Bomb kills three, wounds 21 at Moscow Italian eatery
stories.summary: An explosive device detonated inside an Italian restaurant in Moscow, killing three people and injuring 21 others. Russian media said the blast caused extensive damage and prompted a large emergency response.

stories.headline: Washington wildfires scorch 250k acres, force mass evacuations
stories.summary: Raging fires have burned more than a quarter‑million acres across Washington, prompting emergency declarations and power outages. Thousands of residents have been ordered to evacuate as the blaze spreads.

stories.headline: Pitchfork revisits Pork Soda, the unsettling funk‑metal classic
stories.summary: In its weekly deep‑dive series, Pitchfork examines Pork Soda, the third album by California’s funk‑metal band, noted for its bizarre, gritty sound. The record, despite its oddities, sold over a million copies and remains a polarizing milestone.

stories.headline: California’s data‑deletion law takes effect Aug. 1, tightening privacy rules
stories.summary: The state’s DROP (Delete Online Personal Information) mandate will be enforceable starting August 1, requiring businesses to honor consumer requests to erase personal data. The change aims to give Californians stronger control over their digital footprints.

stories.headline: ‘Flock’ exposes Long Island’s emerging open‑air prison system
stories.summary: The investigative piece ‘Flock’ details how a new surveillance‑heavy housing complex on Long Island functions like an open‑air prison. It highlights concerns over civil liberties as residents face constant monitoring.

stories.headline: Spokane orders Level 3 evacuations as multiple wildfires rage
stories.summary: At least three fires are burning around Spokane, prompting authorities to issue Level 3 evacuation orders that demand immediate departure. Residents are warned that the alerts may be their only notice before conditions worsen.

stories.headline: One‑quarter of babies born premature in Pakistan’s Rehri Goth
stories.summary: In the fishing community of Rehri Goth, roughly 25 % of newborns arrive early, far above national averages. Researchers are investigating environmental and socioeconomic factors to reduce the high preterm birth rate.

stories.headline: ‘Let the Machines In’ argues for embracing AI in daily life
stories.summary: The blog post makes the case that integrating artificial intelligence into everyday tasks can boost productivity and creativity. It also warns of potential pitfalls if adoption is rushed without proper safeguards.

stories.headline: Fire engulfs Indonesia ferry, five dead and 41 missing
stories.summary: A ferry carrying at least 250 passengers caught fire off Madura Island, resulting in five confirmed deaths and 41 people unaccounted for. Rescue teams are battling the blaze while searching for survivors.

stories.headline: Idaho fast‑food restaurant shooting leaves three dead, gunman found dead
stories.summary: A shooting at a fast‑food outlet in Idaho resulted in three fatalities, and police later discovered the suspected shooter’s body near the scene. Authorities are investigating motives and confirming details.

stories.headline: Peruvian Plane Crash Claims 13 Lives
stories.summary: A small tourist plane crashed in Peru, killing 13 people, while flying over the Nazca Lines archaeological site. The incident highlights the risks associated with air travel in remote regions.

stories.headline: TinyNES Console Review: A Niche NES Gaming Experience
stories.summary: The TinyNES console offers a unique gaming experience for enthusiasts of the classic NES, but its limited appeal may not justify the investment for casual gamers. This review provides an in-depth look at the console's features and performance.

stories.headline: NixOS-DGX-Spark: Bringing Nix to NVIDIA's DGX Spark
stories.summary: A new repository provides a way to run Nix on NVIDIA's DGX Spark, offering users a more streamlined experience with the operating system. This development has the potential to improve the performance and efficiency of various applications on the DGX Spark.

stories.headline: Kakehashi: Experimental Project for Running macOS Binaries on Linux ARM
stories.summary: The Kakehashi project aims to enable the execution of macOS binaries on Linux ARM, opening up new possibilities for developers and users. However, the project is still in its experimental stages and requires further testing and refinement.

stories.headline: TP-Link TL-841N Vulnerabilities Exposed
stories.summary: A recent article has revealed several vulnerabilities in the TP-Link TL-841N router, including rooting and firmware analysis issues. These findings highlight the importance of regular security updates and patches for network devices.

stories.headline: Greek Helicopter Crash Claims Two Lives
stories.summary: A tragic incident involving two firefighting helicopters in Greece resulted in the deaths of two crew members, while a British pilot and another Greek crew member survived. The incident serves as a reminder of the risks faced by emergency responders.

stories.headline: Sharing X11 Servers Across Hosts with FamilyWild
stories.summary: A recent article explores the use of FamilyWild to share X11 servers across hosts, providing a convenient solution for users who need to access graphical applications remotely. This approach can simplify the process of remote desktop sharing.

stories.headline: Understanding Cyclospora's Reproductive Cycle
stories.summary: Cyclospora, a parasite responsible for thousands of illnesses in the US this summer, requires time in the human digestive tract to reproduce. Research into the parasite's life cycle can help inform prevention and treatment strategies.

stories.headline: Uganda Unveils Statue of Israel PM's Brother
stories.summary: A statue of Yonatan Netanyahu, the only Israeli soldier to die during the Entebbe rescue mission, was unveiled in Uganda. The tribute honors the bravery and sacrifice of Netanyahu and his comrades.

stories.headline: Renowned Climber Nirmal Purja's Body Recovered
stories.summary: The body of Nirmal Purja, a renowned mountaineer known for scaling the world's 14 highest peaks in record time, was recovered after an avalanche in Pakistan. Purja's achievements and legacy continue to inspire climbers and adventurers worldwide.

stories.headline: Alpine Adventurer Conquers Eight Countries in Record-Breaking Run
stories.summary: Sophie Woods, a seasoned runner, completed the grueling Via Alpina route through treacherous weather conditions, showcasing her endurance and determination. The challenging journey pushed her to her limits, but she emerged victorious.

stories.headline: Introducing F*: A Programming Language for Proofs
stories.summary: F* is a general-purpose programming language designed to facilitate proof-oriented programming, enabling developers to write and verify code with precision and accuracy. This innovative language aims to bridge the gap between programming and formal verification.

stories.headline: Framework 12 Gets a Rusty Hinge Makeover
stories.summary: A resourceful developer created a Linux-based solution to simulate a creaky door effect on the Framework 12, leveraging its hinge angle sensor to create a unique feature. This clever hack showcases the device's versatility and potential for customization.

stories.headline: RISC OS Open Celebrates Two Decades of Open-Source Innovation
stories.summary: RISC OS Open, a pioneering open-source project, marks its 20th anniversary, highlighting two decades of collaborative development and community-driven innovation. This milestone underscores the project's commitment to transparency and community engagement.

stories.headline: The Rise of Solitude as a Lifestyle Choice
stories.summary: A growing number of individuals are embracing solo living, sparking debate and redefining what it means to be alone. These 'loneliness influencers' are challenging societal norms and sparking conversations about the value of solitude.

stories.headline: A Young Scientist Interviews His Hero: A Bird Conservationist
stories.summary: A curious first-grader had the opportunity to interview a renowned bird scientist, gaining insights into the world of conservation science and sparking a passion for learning. This heartwarming exchange highlights the importance of mentorship and curiosity-driven education.
